content: It includes citations for various studies, reports, and publications related to environmental noise, its effects on health, and associated topics. 1. Brink et al. (2018) explored the conversion between various noise exposure indicators, including Leq24h, LDay, LEvening, LNight, Ldn, and Lden. Their work provides both theoretical principles and practical guidance for interpreting these metrics. This study was published in the International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health, Volume 221, Issue 1, pages 54–63. 2. Brink et al. (2016) conducted a field experiment to investigate the effects of scale, question location, response order, and seasonal variations on self-reported noise annoyance using ICBEN scales. The findings were published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, Volume 13, Issue 11. 3. Brown (1987) examined human responses to increased road traffic noise, with findings published in the Journal of Sound and Vibration, Volume 117, Issue 1, pages 69–79. 4. Chang et al. (2014) conducted a cross-sectional study in Taichung, Taiwan, to assess the relationship between road traffic noise frequency and the prevalence of hypertension. The results were published in Environmental Health, Volume 13, Article 37. 5. Eriksson et al. (2010) investigated the gender-specific effects of aircraft noise on the incidence of hypertension. Their study, published in Environmental Research, Volume 110, Issue 8, pages 764–772, highlights the potential cardiovascular risks associated with long-term noise exposure. 6. Clark et al. (2012) analyzed whether traffic-related air pollution could explain the associations between aircraft and road traffic noise exposure and children's health and cognition. This secondary analysis of the UK RANCH project was published in the American Journal of Epidemiology, Volume 176, pages 327–337. 7. Dell and Holmes (2012) evaluated the impact of a hearing conservation program on adolescents' attitudes toward noise. Their findings were published in Noise & Health, Volume 14, Issue 56, pages 39–44. 8. Dratva et al. (2012) studied the relationship between transportation noise and blood pressure in a population-based sample of adults. The results were published in Environmental Health Perspectives, Volume 120, Issue 1, pages 50–55. 9. Eriksson et al. (2014) conducted a prospective study on the long-term effects of aircraft noise exposure on body mass index, waist circumference, and type 2 diabetes. The findings were published in Environmental Health Perspectives, Volume 122, pages 687–694. 10. Floud et al. (2013) examined the effects of aircraft noise exposure on cardiovascular health, with a focus on hypertension and ischemic heart disease. Their study was part of the HYENA project and was published in the British Medical Journal.
